Who Owns the Continuation? AI Music, Creative Direction & Derivative Rights

AI-MUSIC-001 · United States · Educational legal issue-spotting
Legal-review status: Pending independent attorney review

Proposed scenario and evidence boundary

A project creator encounters a recording publicly associated with independent musician Ren. The creator proposes using ChatGPT to analyze musical characteristics and develop a production brief for Suno. The proposed continuation references broad hip-hop production conventions associated with Method Man, Busta Rhymes and the Tical era, without requesting replication of a protected composition, recording, performance or identifiable voice.

This describes a proposed use. It does not report an upload to Suno or a generated derivative track. No audio analysis was performed for this case. A filename or public availability establishes neither authorship nor chain of title, permission or licensing rights. This page includes no source audio, lyrics, screenshots, identifying personal information, stems, imitation audio or playable continuation.

Evidence-status legend

  • Verified platform provision: dated first-party contract or help text; does not verify an account or input's rights.
  • Legal principle: cited U.S. statute or Copyright Office guidance; application remains fact-specific.
  • Interpretation: provisional reasoning for education, subject to attorney review.
  • Proposal: a possible action or agreement, not consent or an executed transfer.
  • Unresolved: essential evidence absent; do not convert it into clearance.

Questions to evaluate

  1. Who owns the original recording, and what documents support that conclusion?
  2. Is its composition owned by the same party?
  3. Would the proposed result contain independent music, an adaptation, or both?
  4. Which human contributions could qualify as authorship?
  5. What rights does Suno contractually assign to paid subscribers?
  6. Which free, paid, extension or enabled Remix workflow applies?
  7. Does commercial permission establish copyright or registration eligibility?
  8. Are sampling, interpolation, imitation, publicity or voice rights implicated?
  9. What collaboration, royalty and administration terms remain to be agreed?
  10. What evidence would support the exact commercial release?

Separate the rights questions

Legal principle — two works. The composition and the recorded performance are separate copyright subjects (Copyright Office Circular 56A, pages 1–2). Establish each ownership record independently; being the named performer does not prove ownership of either. Check writers, performers, producers, publishers, labels and transfers rather than assigning all rights to Ren.

Legal principle — authorship. The Copyright Office's January 2025 Part 2 report, sections II.C–F, distinguishes assistance from generation. Human expression retained in the result, original modifications and sufficiently creative selection or arrangement may qualify; wholly generated material does not. Prompts alone generally do not supply sufficient control under the technology assessed. Creative direction, effort or paying for a service does not itself establish authorship. Inventory actual contributions and disclose/exclude unprotectable AI material as appropriate in registration; commercial permission is not registration eligibility.

Legal principle — authorization. Title 17 sections 101–103 and 106 distinguish adaptation rights from protection for new expression. Owning a new contribution does not transfer the underlying work or authorize its use. Sections 201 and 204 address initial ownership and signed transfers; a collaboration label alone does not establish joint authorship or execute a transfer. Record work-for-hire questions for counsel.

Interpretation — style and copying. General production ideas are distinct from protected expression (section 102(b)). A style reference is not blanket clearance: inspect any retained melody, lyrics, arrangement or recorded sounds. Sampling implicates recording and composition permissions; interpolation can implicate composition rights without copying a master. Section 114(b)'s limits for independently fixed sounds do not clear composition copying. Identifiable voice imitation also raises separate consent, publicity, digital-replica and misleading-endorsement questions. Refer jurisdiction-specific issues to counsel; this case supplies no imitation or fair-use determination.

Interpretation — publication boundary. Discussing these questions publicly does not authorize redistributing or processing the source recording. Keep protected evidence and contracts in a private index. Credit is not permission; permission is not ownership; ownership shares, royalty shares and collection arrangements are separate records.

Platform comparison

Verified platform provisions, checked November 9, 2026: Suno terms revised August 10, effective September 3, 2026, remain displayed. Under “Pro and Premier Accounts,” assignment covers Suno-owned Output from the subscriber's Submissions, subject to terms; copyright vesting is not warranted. Basic output is personal/noncommercial. “Permitted Commercial Use” requires an approved-channel Download within plan allocations and compliant use; download rights survive later subscription changes. Enabled third-party Remixes are contractually joint/equal only insofar as copyright vests, and personal/noncommercial regardless of tier, absent a separate offering. These provisions do not clear third-party inputs. “Using the Service” requires submission authority, including the platform's contemplated processing/model uses.

Verified help guidance: “Who owns an extension?” (edited January 7, 2026) warns against assuming ownership or monetizing another person's extension, or treating a Basic-origin song as cleared through extension. Its shorthand about owning paid outputs is not a guarantee of statutory copyright. The Remix FAQ (edited May 22, 2025) groups Cover, Extend, Reuse and Speed as Remix workflows. It distinguishes another user's song (noncommercial) from one's own paid-origin song remixed while subscribed (commercial eligibility). Apply the later terms and exact feature facts; not every extension is the enabled third-party Remix arrangement. Escalate conflicts or separate-offering claims before use.

Module 6 legal evaluation

Complete this as an extension of the existing capstone, using text only. Add the following copyable record to the rights envelope, then link it in the delivery checklist. Use fictional placeholders for public submissions; keep actual evidence private.

  • Chain of title: asset → author/contributor → agreement/transfer → current holder → proposed licensed use; mark missing links.
  • Composition record / master record: separate authors, holders, evidence IDs and disputed or unknown interests.
  • Human/AI inventory: contribution, person/tool/version, expression retained, edits/arrangement, evidence and uncertain authorship.
  • Terms comparison: free, paid, origin, extension or Remix, plan and feature dates, source URL, revision/effective/retrieval dates, input authority and Download conditions.
  • Permissions checklist: reproduction, analysis, upload and processing, adaptation, samples/interpolation, performance/voice/likeness, distribution, promotion, territory, term and sublicensing; evidence or unresolved status for each.
  • Unresolved-rights register: question, evidence needed, responsible role, next action, release blocker and review date.
  • Attribution/revenue proposal: proposed credit, composition and master interests, fees/royalties, collection administrator, statements and payment schedule; all subject to agreement. Do not fill unknown shares with invented numbers.
  • Decision: proceed / hold / choose another option, exact permitted scope, reasons and evidence that would change it.

Agreement questions for counsel: define contributions and retained rights, processing consent and platform licenses, adaptation authority, approvals, credit, fees, royalties, recoupment, accounting/audit, collection mandates, releases, warranties, disputes, termination and exit. A split sheet or collecting-society registration alone cannot answer every question.

Done: all eight records are linked, unknowns remain visible and the decision identifies the next evidence needed. Use the existing 24-point rubric, unchanged. A substantiated HOLD can be the strongest professional answer and earn full credit; passing the exercise never authorizes a recording's release.

Worked example: hold the proposed continuation

Unresolved: composition holder unknown; master holder unknown. Chain map: publicly associated recording → unidentified contributors/transfers → unknown holders → no documented processing/adaptation license. No signed permissions or account/feature records supplied. Human/AI inventory is proposed only: creator's brief, ChatGPT assistance and potential Suno output; no actual retained expression or output is available to assess.

Verified platform provision: use the dated comparison above, not a claim that an account was used. Proposal: negotiate credit and revenue separately after verifying contributors, ownership and permissions; shares remain unagreed. Register: producer obtains a private evidence index for both chains; counsel reviews processing/adaptation scope and platform compatibility before any upload. No deadline is invented.

Decision — HOLD source processing, continuation and commercial release. Request signed authority from verified holders covering the intended use, contributors' permissions, any required sample/interpolation and voice consents, applicable platform/plan/Download evidence and review of the actual result. A collaboration agreement cannot override platform restrictions by itself. Choose another option: create independent music with original or authorized inputs and reassess it. Ren and all other named artists have not been represented as approving, participating in or endorsing this proposal.

Cross-border and professional review

Unresolved: contributor locations, governing contracts and intended release territories. Other countries' authorship, moral rights, neighboring rights, exceptions and voice/personality rules may differ. U.S. analysis and platform permission do not settle those questions. Identify the relevant territories and obtain qualified local advice rather than exporting this conclusion globally.

Acquisition is not creation: provenance worksheet

Initial investigation record — user-supplied claim, not independently re-inspected here: the example MP4 was described as approximately 26.375 seconds, 720 × 1280, H.264/AAC. No embedded creation-time field was established. The observed filesystem timestamp cannot establish original creation or publication. No actual recording, filename, private timestamp, hash or personal record is published with this account. This addition does not change the proposed-use scenario into an event that occurred.

Keep seven stages separate: original recording creation/publication; acquisition, download and import; proposed ChatGPT analysis/prompting; human decisions/expression; any AI output/adaptation; composition, master, performance and publicity rights; and proposed commercialization, credits, licenses and royalties. The latter stages are proposals or unresolved, not actions verified by a download.

Copyable worksheet: case/artifact ID; source application/reference; original filename, MIME, size and hash where available (private); source-asserted creation and publication times; acquisition/import and observation times; timezone/clock/basis for each; actor claim; custody/transformation events; human/AI contributions; permission/scope; legal hold/release status; verification method; authenticity limitations; unresolved decision and next reviewer. Use unknown when unavailable; append corrections rather than rewriting earlier assertions.

Completed fictional example: AI-MUSIC-001-F1; synthetic text brief, brief.txt, text/plain, bytes/hash recorded in the portable sample; creation/publication unknown; an explicitly fictional observation date is labeled in that sample. A fictional creator proposes original sparse drums without source audio. Human brief expression and proposed AI generation are separate; composition/master holders and processing/adaptation permission for the encountered recording remain unknown. Release: HOLD. Hashing this brief authenticates neither an artist nor the source recording and grants no rights.
